texts: Aulus Vitellius was a Roman emperor who ruled for a brief period in 69 AD, a year known as the Year of the Four Emperors. He came to power after the death of Otho but was eventually defeated by the forces of Vespasian. His reign was marked by political instability and he was known for his extravagant lifestyle.

Aulus Vitellius was a Roman emperor who briefly ruled in 69 CE during the tumultuous Year of the Four Emperors. He came from a prestigious senatorial family and served as a consul under Claudius. Initially a supporter of Galba, he later commanded the legions in Germania and was proclaimed emperor by his troops. Known for his extravagant lifestyle and love of luxurious banquets, Vitellius gained control of Rome after defeating Otho's forces at the First Battle of Bedriacum. His reign was marked by political instability and excessive spending on personal pleasures. He met a violent end when Vespasian's armies entered Rome, where he was captured while attempting to flee to Sicily. He was executed near the Gemonian stairs, and his body was thrown into the Euphrates River, following the ancient Roman custom of disposing of traitors.

Aulus Vitellius was a Roman Emperor from June 68 to December 69 AD, and he was proclaimed Emperor by his troops in Germany after the death of Emperor Nero. Vitellius succeeded Emperor Otho, who reigned briefly after Nero, in the civil war known as the Year of the Four Emperors. He would later be overthrown and executed by forces loyal to Emperor Vespasian, marking the end of the Julio-Claudian and Flavian interregnum, preceding the Flavian dynasty.

He was known for his extravagant lifestyle and heavy banquets, which reportedly drained the Roman treasury. Vitellius came to power after Galba and was succeeded by Otho. His reign was marked by political instability, and he was eventually defeated by Vespasian's forces. Vitellius was known for being particularly cruel, and his downfall came when he was captured and executed by his own troops.
